Moved  Cr Jessica Milne
Seconded  Cr Warren Polley

That Council, having considered:

 

  1. update reports on the native title claim process for Part A of Native Title Determination Application QUD20 of 2019 brought on behalf of the Kabi Kabi First Nation People over parts of Council’s local government area;
  2. confidential and without prejudice correspondence from Crown Law for the State of Queensland to Council’s legal representative dated 9 May 2024; and
  3. an updated draft of the Section 87A Agreement dated 9 May 2024

 

that Council, in its capacity as a respondent party to the claim, resolves to:

 

  1. approve the updated draft of the 87A Agreement as tabled at Council’s special meeting on 14 May 2024 and authorises Council’s legal representative to sign the agreement on Council’s behalf;
  2. consent to the making by the Federal Court of Australia of a native title determination in terms of the draft contained in the Section 87A Agreement for Part A of the claim; and
  3. authorise Council’s Chief Executive Officer to approve any final changes to the updated draft Section 87A Agreement provided they do not depart substantially from the draft tabled at Council’s meeting on 14 May 2024 and do not weaken the protection given to Council’s interest in the determination area; and

 

further resolves that, in respect of the separate confidential ILUA proposed between the Kabi Kabi applicant and the State of Queensland which will cover certain reserves within the native title claim area for which Council is trustee, Council instruct its legal representative to write to Crown Law for the State emphasising Council’s interest in receiving more information about any longer term implications under the ILUA particularly involving potential changes to the reserves.



Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley

  4. In accordance with section 94(1)(b)(i) of the Local Government Act 2009, section 94 of the Local Government Regulation 2012 and section 128A of the Fire and Emergency Services Act 1990, that Council make and levy a special charge (to be known as the “Rural Fire Levy”) of $25.00, on all rateable land to which the overall plan applies, to fund the ongoing provision and maintenance of rural firefighting equipment, operations and buildings for the rural fire brigades that operate throughout the rural areas of the region.

    The overall plan for the Rural Fire Levy special charge is as follows: 
          i.  The service, facility or activity for which the plan is made is the funding of the ongoing provision and maintenance of rural firefighting equipment, operations
              and buildings for the rural fire brigades that operate throughout the rural areas of the region
         ii.  The rateable land to which the plan applies is all rateable land within the region that is liable to pay a Class E Emergency Management Levy (pursuant to Part 3
              of the Fire and Emergency Services Regulation 2011) 
         iii. The estimated cost of carrying out the overall plan is     $292,700
         iv. The estimated time for carrying out the overall plan is one year ending on 30 June 2025. 

    The rateable land to be levied the special charge specifically benefits from the fire emergency response capability that is provided by the rural fire brigades, which capability would be substantially (if not completely) diminished if the rural fire brigades did not receive the funding provided to them by Council as a direct consequence of the levying of the special charge. A pro-rata charge effective from the date of valuation will apply to new assessments created during the financial year.

    • Queensland Pensioner Concession Card (issued by Centrelink or Department of Veterans’ Affairs); or
    • Department of Veterans’ Affairs Health Card for all conditions (Gold Card).

      The pensioner must also be:
    • The owner or life tenant* of the property, which is the principal place of residence and located in Queensland.

Moved  Cr Michael Curran

That Council:
  1. In accordance with Chapter 3 Part 2, Division 2 of the Local Government Act 2009, adopt the 2024-2025 Competition Reform Policy, as tabled.
  2. In accordance with Section 47(7) and 47(9) of the Local Government Act 2009 resolve to apply the Code of Competitive Conduct to its Water Branch as it meets the definition of a significant business activity pursuant to Section 19 (2) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 with the adoption of the Full Cost Pricing business model providing the greatest community net benefit when compared to the Commercialised Business Unit business model.
  3. In accordance with Sections 47(7),and 47(9) of the Local Government Act 2009 that Council resolves to apply the Code of Competitive Conduct to its Waste Management Unit as it meets the definition of a significant business activity pursuant to Section 19 (3) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 with the adoption of the Full Cost Pricing business model providing the greatest community net benefits when compared to the Commercialised Business Unit business model.
  4. That pursuant to Section 47(3)(a) of the Local Government Act 2009, Council continue to apply the Code of Competitive Conduct by applying a Full Cost Pricing business model to its Building Services Unit.

Carried

That Council resolves to approve the exception referred to in Chapter 6 Section 236 (1)(c)(iii) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 allowing Council to dispose of (through leasing) the subject land, other than by tender or auction, to the existing tenant of the land (Lewis Lawrence Stevens, Lorraine Joyce Stevens, Colin Russell Appleton and Nicole Mireille Appleton)

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

M29/7/2024 
Moved  Cr Warren Polley
Seconded  Cr Nadine Jensen

That Council resolves to offer a lease to the current tenant of the land (Lewis Lawrence Stevens, Lorraine Joyce Stevens, Colin Russell Appleton and Nicole Mireille Appleton), over part of Lot 1 RP109088 (Lease N), located at 20 Lobwein Road, Kybong, in Council’s Standard Aerodrome Freehold Lease format to include the following terms and conditions:
a)  Term of Lease – 20 years;
b)  Annual Rental – $4,200.00 (plus GST) per annum plus annual CPI increase at the commencement date of the new lease and yearly on the anniversary of the commencement date of the lease. Market Reviews every 5 years from date of commencement;
c)  Use – Aircraft and/or glider hangar and storage of associated equipment.  Once the special conditions have been fully satisfied, then Flight Training will also be a permitted use;
d)  The Lessee to hold Public Liability Insurance in a sum not less than $20,000,000.00 or such other amount Council shall determine from time to time; and
e)  All costs associated with the preparation, stamping and registration of the Lease are to be borne by the Lessee.
Special conditions:
  1. the Lessee is required to obtain and cover the cost of obtaining the appropriate building classification within twelve (12) months of the execution of this Lease document.  If the correct building classification in accordance with the use of Flight Training is not obtained within this time, then the only use permitted under this Lease is that of aircraft and/or glider hangar and storage of associated equipment; and
  2. once the correct building classification is obtained, a copy is to be provided to council's Property Branch. 

Carried

Moved  Cr Michael Curran

That pursuant to the provision of Section 254J of the Local Government Regulation 2012, council resolves to close the meeting to the public and move into "closed" at 9.06am to consider the following matter:
 
 1. Local Housing Action Plan - Update and Recommendations
 
 This item is in-committee in accordance with the following 

  • sS254J (3)(g) of the Local Government Regulation 2012  - negotiations relating to a commercial matter involving the local government for which a public discussion would be likely to prejudice the interests of the local government;

 This purpose will appear in the Public Minutes. ","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"QUESTION ON NOTICE - Councillor Curran asked if information could be provided on the option of the removal of Council from the State leased land process.  The Manager of Property and Open Space to present a report to a future meeting of Council regarding requirements in handing back trustee lease land to the Queensland Government.  


M11/11/2024 
Moved  Cr Nadine Jensen
Seconded  Cr Gordon Maudsley

That Council:
1. Resolve to approve the exception referred to in Chapter 6, Section 236(1)(c)(iii) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 allowing Council to dispose of (through leasing) the subject land, other than by tender or auction, to the existing tenant of the land.
2. Offers a Trustee Lease to the current lessee's, over part of the land at Lot 40 RP865217 located at Mary's Creek Road, Pie Creek, in Council’s standard commercial trustee lease format, to include the following terms and conditions:
a) Term of Lease: 10 years;
b) Annual Rental: Rent will be reviewed annually on the anniversary of the Commencement Date and increased 3% pa in accordance with “Gympie Regional Council’s Fees and Charges” for a Commercial Lease Agreement, commencing at $7,305.05 inclusive of GST;
c) Use: Environmental/Buffer Zone;
d) The Lessee is to hold public liability insurance in a sum not less than $20,000,000.00 or such other amount that Council shall determine from time to time;
e) All costs associated with the preparation, stamping and registration of the Lease are to be borne by the Lessee.
f) The lease area to be maintained to ensure a sufficient fire break area is included.
Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Officers Recommendation
That Council, as Assessment Manager, REFUSE the Development Application for a Development Permit for the Material Change of Use to establish a Function Facility and Short Term Accommodation on land at 24 Amy Street and Lady Mary Terrace, Gympie QLD 4570, for the following reasons: 
 
  1. The proposed development conflicts with the Strategic Framework of the Planning Scheme, and in particular: 
    1. Table 3.1, Element (1), Specific Outcome (g) in that the proposed development does not facilitate the increase in population density on land in close proximity to the town centre. 
    2. Table 3.1, Element (1), Specific Outcome (h) in that the proposed development does not facilitate higher density residential development in close proximity to the Gympie City centre. 
    3. Table 3.5, Element (2), Specific Outcome (d) in that the proposed development does not provide for a housing choice including traditional detached houses, small lot houses, townhouses, duplexes and unit development.  
    4. Table 3.6, Element (1), Specific Outcome (a) in that the proposed development increases non-local traffic on local roads, and does not mitigate or minimise the impact associated with the non-local traffic. 
    5. Table 3.6, Element (5), Specific Outcome (a) in that the proposed development has not demonstrated that the existing urban infrastructure has the capacity to accommodate the increased loading associated with the development. 
  2. The proposed development conflicts with relevant provisions of the Residential Choice Zone Code, as outlined below: 
    1. The proposed development conflicts with the purpose of the Residential Choice Zone Code as it does not provide for a range and mix of dwelling types, including dwelling houses and multiple dwellings. Nor does the proposed development provide for small-scale services and facilities that cater for local residents. 
    2. The proposed development conflicts with Overall Outcome (3)(d) in that the non-residential land use does not directly support the day-to-day needs of the residential community. 
    3. The proposed development conflicts with Overall Outcome (3)(d) in that the non-residential land use detracts from the residential amenity of the area.
    4. The proposed development conflicts with Overall Outcome (3)(g) in that it does not achieve a high level of amenity for residents that is reflective of the intended area.
  3. The proposed development conflicts with the relevant provisions of the District Centre Zone Code, as outlined below:
    1. The proposed development conflicts with Overall Outcome (3)(d) in that it does not provide for a high level of amenity and is not reflective of the surrounding residential character of the area.
  4. The proposed development conflicts with the relevant provisions of the Infrastructure and Operational Work (excluding Advertising Device) code, as outlined below:
    1. The proposed development conflicts with Overall Outcome (3)(b) in that it does not facilitate the safe and efficient operation of infrastructure in a manner that meets the community’s expectations.
    2. The proposed development conflicts with Overall Outcome (3)(b) in that it does not prevent unacceptable off-site impacts or reduce the whole of lifecycle costs, including ongoing maintenance costs of transport infrastructure.
    3. The proposed development conflicts with Overall Outcome (3)(c) in that it does not provide vehicle parking that reflects the nature and intensity of the proposal.
  5. The proposed development cannot be conditioned to comply with the aforementioned matters as it would require substantial changes, resulting in a different development from what was originally applied for.
  6. The proposed development is inconsistent with the reasonable community expectations for the subject site having regard to its context and the surrounding neighbourhood.
  7. No relevant matters exist to support the proposed development being approved despite the aforementioned conflicts with the Planning Scheme.

M19/11/2024 
Moved  Cr Michael Curran
Seconded  Cr Nadine Jensen

That Council lay the development application on the table and request the Applicant to provide further information as requested previously by council's development assessment team (being, at a minimum, the provision of a comprehensive traffic impact statement addressing the shortfall of onsite car parking, and a noise impact assessment confirming that no adverse amenity impacts will be imposed upon surrounding residential properties as a result of the proposed development).  An update report to be tabled at the next Ordinary Meeting of Council scheduled for 18 December 2024.
Carried

Meeting resumed at 12.45pm

Cr Curran declared a conflict of interest in relation to item 10.9 "Proposed amendment to the agreement with Rattler Railway Ltd" to be discussed in Closed session of Council. 

Cr Curran advised as a shareholder in a syndicate for partial ownership (estimated two per cent) of a thoroughbred horse, with a board member from the Rattler Railway Ltd, also be part of this syndicate, conflict of interest declared. However, Cr Curran advised that he believed he would be able to remain impartial in relation to the discussion of this matter and asked to be permitted to stay in the room and participate in the discussion and vote of this matter.

Moved  Cr Warren Polley

Carried

That in relation to development approval for Material Change of Use (2022-0041) - Transport Depot (Removalist's Depot) and Warehouse (Storage of Shipping Containers), Council as Assessment Manager decide the change representations and issue a negotiated decision notice, as follows: 
 (i) for Council's consideration regarding hours of operation
 (ii) amend condition 10 to read:
 Carlson Road is to be upgraded to achieve an ultimate Rural Local Rural Road design standard, from the eastern property boundary of Lot 2 on RP144491 to a point no closer than 50m to the north west of the northern access location to Lot 2 on RP144491. Specifically, the following works are to be undertaken in accordance with plans and specifications approved by Council:
 a) Carlson Road is to be widened to a 7.0 metre wide formation and sealed to 6.0 metre width consisting of two (2) by 3.0 metre wide lanes and two (2) by 0.5 metre wide shoulders with associated drainage works. 
 (iii) amend condition 21 to read:
 The approved development is to be limited to the existing cleared areas.

a) Carlson Road is to be widened to a 7.0 metre wide formation and sealed to 6.0 metre width consisting of two (2) by 3.0 metre wide lanes and two (2) by 0.5 metre wide shoulders with associated drainage works. 
(iii) amend condition 21 to read:
The approved development is to be limited to the existing cleared areas. 
Carried

That Council:

  1. Resolve to approve the exception referred to in Chapter 6, Section 236(1)(c)(iii) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 allowing Council to dispose of (through leasing) the subject land, other than by tender or auction, to the existing tenant of the land.
  2. Offers a Trustee Lease to the Gympie Historic Auto Club Inc. over Part of Lot 140 on CP MCH4786 Lease Area C, in Council’s standard community lease format, to include the following terms and conditions:
  • Term of Lease: 10 years;
  • Annual Rental: Rent will be reviewed annually on the anniversary of the Commencement Date and increased in accordance with “Gympie Regional Council’s Fees and Charges” for a Community Lease Agreement, currently $136.00 inclusive of GST per lease per annum;
  • Use: Community Recreation Facility;
  • The Lessee is to hold public liability insurance in a sum not less than $20,000,000.00 or such other amount that Council shall determine from time to time; and
  • All costs associated with the preparation, stamping and registration of the Lease are to be borne by the Lessee up to $1500.00

Moved  Cr Gordon Maudsley
Seconded  Cr Warren McEwan

That Council:
1. Approves the exception referred to in Chapter 6 Section 236(1)(c)(iii) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 allowing Council to dispose of (through leasing) the subject land, other than by tender or auction, to the existing tenant of the land.
2. Offers a Freehold Lease to Community Action Inc. to include the following terms and conditions:
  1. Term of lease - sixteen (16) months
  2. Annual rental - Rent will be reviewed annually on the anniversary of the commencement date and increased in accordance with 'Gympie Regional Council's Fees and Charges' for a community lease agreement, currently $136.00 inclusive of GST
  3. Use - Affordable accommodation
  4. Public Liability Insurance - The Lessee to hold Public Liability Insurance in a sum not less than $20,000,000 or such other amount that Council shall determine from time to time
  5. Costs - all cost associated with the preparation, stamping and registration of the lease are to be borne by Council.
Carried

Moved  Cr Jessica Milne

That pursuant to the provision of Section 254J of the Local Government Regulation 2012, council resolves to close the meeting to the public and move into "closed" at 11.48am to consider the following matters:

1. Proposed Lease Renewal – Management of Pensioner Units
  • under regulation 254J(3)(i) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 – a matter the local government is required to keep confidential under law or formal arrangement with the Commonwealth or State
 2. Proposed Disposal – 258 East Deep Creek Road, East Deep Creek
  • under regulation 275(1)(e) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 - contracts proposed to be made by it.
  • under regulation s275(1)(h) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 - other business for which a public discussion would be likely to prejudice the interests of the local government or someone else, or enable a person to gain a financial advantage.
 3. Planning Investigation Area
  • under regulation 275(1)(h) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 - other business for which a public discussion would be likely to prejudice the interests of the local government or someone else or enable a person to gain a financial advantage.

This purpose will appear in the Public Minutes. Further, that in relation to the provisions of Section 171 of the Local Government Act 2009, Council resolves that following the closing of the meeting to the public and the moving ‘into closed’ that all matters and all documents (whether in hard copy, electronic, optical, visual or magnetic form) discussed, raised, tabled and/or considered whilst the meeting is closed and ‘in committee’, are confidential to the Council and the Council wishes to keep them confidential.
Carried

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Officers Recommendation
That Council, as Assessment Manager, REFUSE the Development Application for a Development Permit for the Material Change of Use to establish a Function Facility and Short-Term Accommodation on land at 24 Amy Street and Lady Mary Terrace, Gympie QLD 4570, for the following reasons: 
 
(a) The proposed development conflicts with the Strategic Framework of the Planning Scheme, and in particular: a. Table 3.1, Element (1), Specific Outcome (g) in that the proposed development does not facilitate the increase in population density on land in close proximity to the town centre. 
b. Table 3.1, Element (1), Specific Outcome (h) in that the proposed development does not facilitate higher density residential development in close proximity to the Gympie City centre. 
c. Table 3.5, Element (2), Specific Outcome (d) in that the proposed development does not provide for a housing choice including traditional detached houses, small lot houses, townhouses, duplexes and unit development. 
d. Table 3.6, Element (1), Specific Outcome (a) in that the proposed development increases non-local traffic on local roads, and does not mitigate or minimise the impact associated with the non-local traffic. 
e. Table 3.6, Element (5), Specific Outcome (a) in that the proposed development has not demonstrated that the existing urban infrastructure has the capacity to accommodate the increased loading associated with the development. 

(b) The proposed development conflicts with relevant provisions of the Residential Choice Zone Code, as outlined below: 
a. The proposed development conflicts with the purpose of the Residential Choice Zone Code as it does not provide for a range and mix of dwelling types, including dwelling houses and multiple dwellings. Nor does the proposed development provide for small-scale services and facilities that cater for local residents. 
b. The proposed development conflicts with Overall Outcome (3)(d) in that the non-residential land use does not directly support the day-to-day needs of the residential community. 
 
(c) The proposed development conflicts with the relevant provisions of the Infrastructure and Operational Work (excluding Advertising Device) code, as outlined below: 
a. The proposed development conflicts with Overall Outcome (3)(b) in that it does not facilitate the safe and efficient operation of infrastructure in a manner that meets the community’s expectations. 
b. The proposed development conflicts with Overall Outcome (3)(b) in that it does not prevent unacceptable off-site impacts or reduce the whole of lifecycle costs, including ongoing maintenance costs of transport infrastructure. 
c. The proposed development conflicts with Overall Outcome (3)(c) in that it does not provide vehicle parking that reflects the nature and intensity of the proposal. 
 
(d) The proposed development is inconsistent with the reasonable community expectations for the subject site having regard to its context and the surrounding neighbourhood. 
(e) No ‘relevant matters’ exist to support the proposed development being approved despite the aforementioned conflicts with the Planning Scheme. 

Due to no Mover or Second this motion lapsed, and an alternative motion was provided. 

M16/6/2025 
Moved  Cr Michael Curran
Seconded  Cr Warren Polley

That Council approve Development Application (2024-0225) for a Material Change of Use for a Function Facility and Short-Term Accommodation at 24 Amy Street and Lady Mary Terrace, Gympie (Lot 24 and Lot 26 on SP314400), subject to reasonable and relevant conditions to be determined by Director Community Sustainability, including the implementation of the recommendations contained in the submitted acoustic report.

Carried

Moved  Cr Jessica Milne
Seconded  Cr Warren Polley

That Council:
  1. Resolve to approve the exception referred to in Chapter 6, Section 236(1)(c)(iii) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 allowing Council to dispose of (through leasing) the subject land, other than by tender or auction, to the existing tenant of the land. 
  2. Resolve to offer a Freehold Lease to the Gympie Motorcycle Club Inc. over Part of Lot 2 on SP246429 - Lease area F, in Council’s standard community lease format, to include the following terms and conditions: 
  • Term of Lease: 5 years; 
  • Annual Rental: Rent will be reviewed annually on the anniversary of the Commencement Date and increased in accordance with “Gympie Regional Council’s Fees and Charges” for a Community Lease Agreement, currently $136.00 inclusive of GST per annum; 
  • Use: Storage Shed; 
  • The Lessee is to hold public liability insurance in a sum not less than $20,000,000.00 or such other amount that Council shall determine from time to time; and
  • All costs associated with the preparation, stamping and registration of the Lease are to be borne by the Lessee up to $1500.00 plus GST.

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Original Officer Recommendation: 
That Council consider the following motions with the associated rationale to be submitted to the Local Government Association of Queensland:

Motion 1: Amend the Electoral Act 1992 to include provisions to restrict any person from canvassing for votes using loud speaker, amplifier, physical material or otherwise at voting centres or polling places.

Rationale:  The effect of this motion would be to negate the handing out of content or canvasing for votes while people are entering a polling place. This motion would still allow for the provision of information but in a static manner on a stand or table. This would replicate the core similarities of the Covid- 19 restrictions that were in place during the respective election period. This would allow for a more pleasant voting experience and would reduce some anxiety voters may have around the voting process allowing them to be able to make a more levelheaded decision when choosing who to vote for without feeling pressured to vote for the party who was the most present on the day at the voting centre or polling place.

M10/7/2025 
Moved  Cr Michael Curran
Seconded  Cr Nadine Jensen

LGAQ Motion 1 be laid on the table for further discussion at a future meeting. 

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

M11/7/2025 
Moved  Cr Allona Lahn
Seconded  Cr Gordon Maudsley

Motion 2: That funding for Local Government Authorities is reformed into an annualised funding model.

Rationale: An annualised funding model would allow Council to be more forward thinking when making decisions regarding expenditure of funds for major infrastructure improvements and projects. Rather than the current sporadic grant model having an annualised funding model would allow Council to be able to make an informed decision on what can be achieved that year.

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

I, Cr Warnes inform this meeting that despite previously stating a Declarable Conflict of Interest on this matter, due to having a personal interest in the matter and at the time that interest was due to having access to information that I believe was not widely shared with the other elected members.

As such, I wish to participate in the discussion and vote in relation to this matter, I acknowledge that eligible (non-conflicted) Councillors must now determine, pursuant to section 150ES of the Local Government Act 2009, whether I:

  • Must leave the meeting, including any area set aside for the public, and stay away from the meeting while the eligible (non-conflicted) Councillors discuss and vote on the matter.

  1. In accordance with section 94(1)(b)(i) of the Local Government Act 2009, section 94 of the Local Government Regulation 2012 and section 128A of the Fire and Emergency Services Act 1990, that Council make and levy a special charge (to be known as the “Rural Fire Levy”) of $25.00, on all rateable land to which the overall plan applies, to fund the ongoing provision and maintenance of rural firefighting equipment, operations and buildings for the rural fire brigades that operate throughout the rural areas of the region.

    The overall plan for the Rural Fire Levy special charge is as follows: 
          i.  The service, facility or activity for which the plan is made is the funding of the ongoing provision and maintenance of rural firefighting equipment, operations
              and buildings for the rural fire brigades that operate throughout the rural areas of the region
         ii.  The rateable land to which the plan applies is all rateable land within the region that is liable to pay a Class E Emergency Management Levy (pursuant to Part 3
              of the Fire and Emergency Services Regulation 2011) 
         iii. The estimated cost of carrying out the overall plan is $295,925
         iv. The estimated time for carrying out the overall plan is one year ending on 30 June 2026. 

    The rateable land to be levied the special charge specifically benefits from the fire emergency response capability that is provided by the rural fire brigades, which capability would be substantially (if not completely) diminished if the rural fire brigades did not receive the funding provided to them by Council as a direct consequence of the levying of the special charge.   10.     Pensioners must hold one of the following concession cards:

Moved  Cr Allona Lahn
Seconded  Cr Gordon Maudsley

That Council consider the following motions with the associated rationale to be submitted to the Local Government Association of Queensland:

Motion 1 - The LGAQ calls upon the state Government to amend the Electoral Act 1992 to include a provision for local government/councils to have the option to opt out of physical canvassing at local government elections and/or have the option to instigate and implement a no canvassing lane (where possible) giving the voters the option to interact or not with candidates and volunteers whilst voting at polling booths.
 
This would require the need for an entry lane where voters can be canvassed and/or one without. The guidelines and principles used during the 2020 election could be adopted where council chooses, allowing people the freedom to vote without the intimidation and inconvenience of being canvassed.
 
Rationale: The effect of this motion would be to negate the handing out of content or canvasing for votes while people are entering a polling place. This motion would still allow for the provision of information but in a static manner on a stand or table. This would replicate the core similarities of the Covid- 19 restrictions that were in place during the respective election period. This would allow for a more pleasant voting experience and would reduce some anxiety voters may have around the voting process.
Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

Moved  Cr Michael Curran

That Council:
1. Approves the rescinding of Resolution M11/05/2025 at the May Ordinary Meeting to dispose of the (through leasing) the subject land and considers this revised report and recommendation.
2. In accordance with Section 235 (a) and (b) of the Local Government Regulation 2012, Council resolves that it is satisfied that due to the unique combination of local knowledge and expertise possessed by both Trustee Lessee's:
  1. To approve the annual payment to the Trustee Lessee's in the amount of $80,000.00 plus GST to be paid on the anniversary of the lease commencement and increased each year by CPI for the management of the complex, as the Trustee Lessee's are the only suppliers reasonably available to manage the Gympie Showgrounds: and
  2. The special knowledge, experience and success that the Trustee Lessee's have acquired and demonstrated, it would be impractical or disadvantageous for Council to invite quotes or tenders instead of engaging the Trustee Lessee's to manage the showgrounds.
3. Approves the exception referred to in Chapter 6 Section 236(1)(c)(iii) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 allowing Council to dispose of (through leasing) the subject land, other than by tender or auction, to the existing tenant of the land.
4. Offers a Trustee Lease to the Gympie District Show Society Inc. and Gympie Turf Club Inc. in Council's standard trustee community lease format, to include the following terms and conditions:
  1. Term of Lease - 10 years
  2. Annual Rental - Rent will be reviewed annually on the anniversary of the commencement date and increased in accordance with 'Gympie Regional Council's Fees and Charges' for a community lease agreement, currently $141.00 inclusive of GST;
  3. Use - Recreation, Racecourse and Showgrounds
  4. Public Liability Insurance - The Trustee Lessee to hold Public Liability Insurance in a sum not less than $20,000,000.00 or such other amount that Council shall determine from time to time;
  5. Costs - All costs associated with the preparation, stamping and registration of the lease are to be borne by the Trustee Lessee up to a maximum of $1,500.00.


Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

Moved  Cr Jessica Milne

Resolution 1
In accordance with the ‘Gympie Regional Council Process for Making Local Laws’ adopted on 11/9/2013, the Council hereby resolves to propose to make the following:
  • Amendment Local Law No. 1 (Miscellaneous) 2026
  • Amendment Subordinate Local Law No. 1 (Miscellaneous) 2026
  • Subordinate Local Law No. 1 (Administration) 2026
  • Local Law No. 7 (Aerodromes) 2026
  • Subordinate Local Law No. 7 (Aerodromes) 2026

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

M34/10/2025 
Moved  Cr Warren Polley
Seconded  Cr Shane Warnes

Resolution 2
The Council hereby resolves to undertake community consultation, comprising:
  • publicly advertising the proposed local laws and subordinate local laws on the Council’s website for a period of at least 60 days;
  • inviting and considering submissions by the public about the proposed local laws and subordinate local laws.

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

M35/10/2025 
Moved  Cr Jessica Milne
Seconded  Cr Warren McEwan

Resolution 3
The Council hereby resolves:
  • it has reviewed the proposed local laws and subordinate local laws to identify any possible anti-competitive provisions, pursuant to section 38 of the Local Government Act 2009;
  • the following proposed local laws contain possible anti-competitive provisions:
    1. Amendment Local Law No. 1 (Miscellaneous) 2026
    2. Amendment Subordinate Local Law No. 1 (Miscellaneous) 2026
    3. Subordinate Local Law No. 1 (Administration) 2026
    4. Local Law No. 7 (Aerodromes) 2026
    5. Subordinate Local Law No. 7 (Aerodromes) 2026
  • a Public Interest Review will be conducted for the possible anti-competitive provisions through advertising a Public Interest Review Consultation Paper to businesses and members of the public during the public consultation period for the local laws. 

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

Moved  Cr Michael Curran

That pursuant to the provision of section 254J of the Local Government Regulation 2012 Council resolves to close the meeting to the public and move into "closed" at 11.28am to consider the following matters:

For futher discussion 8.1 was moved into closed with reference to:
  • s254J(3)(g) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 - negotiations relating to a commercial matter involving the local government for which a public discussion would be likely to prejudice the interests of the local government.

1. Requests For Rating Concessions
  • s254J(3)(d) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 - rating concessions.

2. Temporary Local Planning Instrument
  • s254J(3)(e) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 - legal advice obtained by the local government or legal proceedings involving the local government including, for example, legal proceedings that may be taken by or against the local government

3. Proposed Disposal - 9 Violet Street, Gympie
  • s275(1)(e) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 - contracts proposed to be made by it.
  • s275(1)(h) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 - other business for which a public discussion would be likely to prejudice the interests of the local government or someone else or enable a person to gain a financial advantage.

4. Tender award RFT000022 T167 - Separable Portions 7-10
  • s254J(3)(c) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 - the local government’s budget
  • s254J(3)(g) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 - negotiations relating to a commercial matter involving the local government for which a public discussion would be likely to prejudice the interests of the local government.

5. LATE ITEM - Legal Services - Procurement Exception
  • s254J(3)(e) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 - legal advice obtained by the local government or legal proceedings involving the local government including, for example, legal proceedings that may be taken by or against the local government.
  • s254J(3)(g) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 - negotiations relating to a commercial matter involving the local government for which a public discussion would be likely to prejudice the interests of the local government.

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley

Moved  Cr Nadine Jensen

Recommendation 1:  
  • That Council resolves to endorse the following pledge:
  • Gympie Regional Council Pledge Against Domestic, Family and Sexual Violence 
  • Gympie Regional Council says NO to Domestic and Family Violence and Sexual Violence.
  • Gympie Regional Council says YES to relationships and communities that are safe, respectful and free from violence.
  • Gympie Regional Council will work within our organisation and in partnership with government, community and business sectors to raise awareness against Family and Domestic Violence and Sexual Violence.
  • Gympie Regional Council will use our information networks and available resources to support violence prevention campaigns and programs.

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

M15/12/2025 
Moved  Cr Jessica Milne
Seconded  Cr Nadine Jensen

Recommendation 2:  
In regard to understanding and raising awareness about the prevention of domestic and family violence and sexual violence, Council resolves to:
  1. Endorse Phase 1-3 actions outlined in this report to be implemented within this term of Council, subject to available resources; and
  2. Request that officers report on the prevention activities that Council is involved with, as part of standard corporate reporting (e.g. Quarterly Directorate reports).

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Original Officer Recommendation:
That Council amend its Resolution from the Ordinary Meeting held on 12 November 2025 Item 7.1 RENEWAL OF TEMPORARY LOCAL PLANNING INSTRUMENT - BIODIVERSITY PROTECTION to the following:
  1. Proposes to make a Temporary Local Planning Instrument (TLPI) titled "Protection of Biodiversity Values" as attached to this report.
  2. Authorises the Chief Executive Officer to write to the Minister for State Development, Infrastructure and Planning to seek approval of the Proposed TLPI in accordance with Chapter 3, Part 2, Section 8.1 of the Minister’s Guidelines and Rules. 
  3. Requests, on the basis that the Minister for State Development, Infrastructure and Planning gives the Council a notice stating that the Minister approves the making of the Proposed TLPI, the Chief Executive Officer bring forward a Council report to adopt the TLPI in accordance with Chapter 3, Part 2, Section 9 of the Minister’s Guidelines and Rules as soon as reasonably practicable.
  4. Commits to workshopping the policy position for primary production activities on rural land in relation to biodiversity values in the context of the new planning scheme.
  5. Request that the report relating to this recommendation be publicly released, subject to the removal of any legal advice.

M11/12/2025 
Moved  Cr Jessica Milne
Seconded  Mayor Glen Hartwig

That Council amend its Resolution from the Ordinary Meeting held on 12 November 2025 Item 7.1 RENEWAL OF TEMPORARY LOCAL PLANNING INSTRUMENT - BIODIVERSITY PROTECTION to the following:
  1. Proposes to make a Temporary Local Planning Instrument (TLPI) titled "Protection of Biodiversity Values" as attached to this report.
  2. Authorises the Chief Executive Officer to write to the Minister for State Development, Infrastructure and Planning to seek approval of the Proposed TLPI in accordance with Chapter 3, Part 2, Section 8.1 of the Minister’s Guidelines and Rules. 
  3. Requests, on the basis that the Minister for State Development, Infrastructure and Planning gives the Council a notice stating that the Minister approves the making of the Proposed TLPI, the Chief Executive Officer bring forward a Council report to adopt the TLPI in accordance with Chapter 3, Part 2, Section 9 of the Minister’s Guidelines and Rules as soon as reasonably practicable.
  4. Commits to considering the policy position for primary production activities on rural land in relation to biodiversity values to address the hinderances and promote the rights of rural land holders in the context of the new planning scheme.
  5. Request that the report relating to this recommendation be publicly released, subject to the removal of any legal advice.

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

That Council:
  1. Approves the exception referred to in Chapter 6 Section 236(1)(c)(iv) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 allowing Council to dispose of a valuable non-current asset other than by tender or auction if - 
    1. The land is not suitable to be offered for disposal by tender or auction for a particular reason; and 
    2. There is not another person who owns other adjoining land who wishes to acquire the land; and 
    3. It is in the public interest to dispose of the land wcuithout tender or auction; and d) the disposal is otherwise in accordance with sound contracting principles.
  2. Delegates authority for the Chief Executive Officer to enter into a contract for the market value for the subject property and complete all necessary documentation to complete the transfer to the proposed buyer.

Carried

  2. Council acknowledge that Council officers will continue to negotiate in acquiring property by agreement, and if negotiations are successful enter into a contract of purchase on terms satisfactory to the Chief Executive Officer;
  3. If the process of acquisition, is unsuccessful, that Council delegate authority to the Chief Executive Officer in accordance with section 257(1) of the Local Government Act 2009 to undertake activities under the sections 7, 8 and 9 of the Acquisition of Land Act 1967, including hearing objections under section 8, and, if no objections to the Notice of Intention to Resume are received, to decide whether to make an application to the Minister under section 9 of the Acquisition of Land Act 1967;
  4.   5. All reasonable costs of survey, valuation fees, legal costs, registration, stamp duty and all other fees associated with the acquisition be at Council’s expense.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Procedural Motion 
Moved Cr Jessica Milne

1. For the document 'Protection of Rural Land Biodiversity Values' to be tabled at this meeting for inclusion and adequate consideration.

Original Officer Recommendation:
That Council:
1. Adopt the new Temporary Local Planning Instrument - Protection of Biodiversity Values as shown in Attachment 3 in accordance with the advice of the Minister dated 16 January 2026,
2. Resolve to prepare an additional TLPI (Protection of Biodiversity Values in the Rural Zone) applying to the rural zone that would identify and protect the wetland and waterways within the rural zone from inappropriate development, and,
3. Commit to workshop the policy position for primary production activities on rural land in relation to biodiversity values in the context of the new planning scheme.

Question on Notice
Councillor Curran requested information from Manager - Compliance on the number of compliance actions undertaken in relation to the Temporary Local Planning Instrument.

M1/2/2026 
Moved  Cr Michael Curran
Seconded  Cr Gordon Maudsley

That Council:
1. Adopt the new Temporary Local Planning Instrument - Protection of Biodiversity Values as shown in Attachment 3 in accordance with the advice of the Minister dated 16 January 2026.
2. Resolve to make an additional TLPI 2/2026 - Protection of Rural Land Biodiversity Values - as tabled at the meeting, applying to the rural zone that would identify and protect the wetland and waterways within the rural zone from inappropriate development and,
3. Request the Minister for Planning, under Section 9(4) of the Planning Act 2016, make 23 February 2026 the effective date for TLPI 2/2026 - Protection of Rural Land Biodiversity Values.
4. Commit to workshop the policy position for primary production activities on rural land in relation to biodiversity values in the context of the new planning scheme.

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"M17/4/2026 
Moved  Cr Gordon Maudsley
Seconded  Cr Jess Milne

That Council:
  1. Approves the exception referred to in Chapter 6 Section 236 (1)(c)(iii) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 allowing Council to dispose of (through leasing) the subject land, other than by tender or auction, to the existing tenant of the land.
  2. Offers a Freehold Lease to the NCACCH in Council’s standard Freehold Lease format, to include the following terms and conditions:
  1. Term of Lease – 5 years.
  2. Rental - $1950.52 per month (excluding GST) and increased annually on the anniversary of the commencement date by a fixed percentage of 3% annually.
  3. Use – Community Health Centre.
  4. PLI – The Lessee to hold Public Liability Insurance in a sum not less than $20,000,000.00 or such other amount that Council Shall determine from time to time.
  5. Legal Costs – All legal costs associated with the preparation and stamping of the Lease are to be borne by the Lessee up to a maximum of $1,500.00.
  6. Survey Costs - (if applicable) Council will contribute fifty percent (50%) of the cost of the survey plan. The Lessee will be responsible for the remaining cost of the survey plan.
  7. Other Costs – All costs associated with the registration of the lease are to be borne by the Lessee.

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

FOR: Councillor Milne
AGAINST: Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley


M7/5/2026 
Moved Cr Mick Curran
Seconded Cr Shane Warnes

That Council:

  1. Approves the exception referred to in Chapter 6, section 236(1)(c)(iii) of the Local Government Regulation 2012, allowing Council to dispose of the subject land by way of lease, other than by tender or auction, to the existing tenant of the land, being the Australian Institute of Country Music Inc. (AICM);

  2. Offers a Freehold Community Lease to the Australian Institute of Country Music Inc. for the Council-owned facility located at 26 Channon Street, Gympie, in Council’s standard Freehold Community Lease format, on the following terms and conditions:

    a. Term – An initial term of three (3) years with two further options of three (3) years and four (4) years respectively;

    b. Annual Rental – Rent to be reviewed annually on the anniversary of the commencement date and increased in accordance with Gympie Regional Council’s adopted Fees and Charges for a Community Lease Agreement;

    c. Use – Arts and cultural venue including musical education, training, research, live performances, and associated community arts and cultural activities; 

    d. Public Liability Insurance – The Lessee to hold Public Liability Insurance in an amount not less than $20,000,000.00, or such other amount as Council may determine from time to time;

    e. Costs – All costs associated with the preparation, stamping, and registration of the lease are to be borne by the Lessee up to a maximum contribution by Council of $1,500 plus GST;

  3. Notes that the proposed lease will replace the existing lease arrangement, which is approximately 20 years old, with an updated lease agreement reflecting current Council lease management standards, obligations, and operational requirements (including third party hire of the facility and maximising community use and activation); and
  4. Authorises the Chief Executive Officer to finalise and execute all necessary documentation associated with the lease arrangement.


Carried

Moved Mayor Glen Hartwig
Seconded Cr Jess Milne

That Council:
1. Notes the proposed changes by the Federal Government to Disaster Recovery funding arrangements; and
2. Expresses its strong and united opposition to the proposed changes on the basis that they will have significant and adverse impacts on disaster-affected regional communities, including within the Gympie Local Government Area; and
3. Advocates to the Federal Government to reconsider and reverse these proposed changes to ensure ongoing equitable, timely and adequate disaster recovery support for regional councils and communities; and
4. Authorises the Mayor to write to the Prime Minister, relevant Federal Ministers, and local Federal Members of Parliament, outlining Council’s position and concerns; and
5. Supports collaboration with the State Government and other local governments and peak bodies (including the Local Government Association of Queensland) to collectively advocate against these changes; and

Original Officer Recommendation:

Councillors endorse granting Lot 6 CP894551 Part A tenure to Rainbow Beach Amateur Anglers Inc. and Lot 6 CP894551 Part B tenure to Cooloola Coastcare Association Inc. outside of a formal Invitation for Tenure process under the Community Leasing Policy.


Proposed Alternative Recommendation:
 That Council:
  1. Approves the exception referred to in Chapter 6 Section 236(1)(b)(ii) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 allowing Council to dispose of (through leasing) the subject land, other than by tender or auction, to a community organisation.
  2. Endorses granting part-tenure of Lot 6 CP894551 to Rainbow Beach Amateur Anglers Inc. and part-tenure of Lot 6 CP894551 to Cooloola Coastcare Association Inc. outside a formal Invitation for Tenure process provided for under the Community Leasing Policy.
  3. Offers a Trustee Lease to Rainbow Beach Amateur Anglers Inc. in Council’s standard trustee community lease format for part-tenure, to include the following terms and conditions:
    1. Term of Lease – 10 years;
    2. Annual Rental – Rent will be reviewed annually on the anniversary of the commencement date and increased in accordance with ‘Gympie Regional Council’s Fees and Charges’ for a community lease agreement, currently $141.00 inclusive of GST;
    3. The specific tenure area within the subject lot is to be negotiated between Council and Rainbow Beach Amateur Anglers Inc;  
    4. Use – Recreational Facility;
    5. PLI – The Trustee Lessee to hold Public Liability Insurance in a sum not less than $20,000,000.00 or such other amount that Council shall determine from time to time;
    6. Costs – All costs associated with the preparation, stamping and registration of the lease are to be borne by the Trustee Lessee up to a maximum of $1,500.00;
    7. Survey fees will be divided equally between Gympie Regional Council and Rainbow Beach Amateur Anglers Inc.
 
  1. Offers a 12 month Due Diligence Licence Agreement to Cooloola Coastcare Association Inc. in Council’s standard due diligence licence agreement format for part-tenure, to include the following terms and conditions:
    1. Term of Licence Agreement – 1 year;
    2. Annual Rental – Rent will be reviewed annually on the anniversary of the commencement date and increased in accordance with ‘Gympie Regional Council’s Fees and Charges’ for a community lease agreement, currently $141.00 inclusive of GST;
    3. The specific tenure area within the subject lot is to be negotiated between Council and Cooloola Coastcare Association Inc.  
    4. Use – Storage;
    5. PLI – The Licensee to hold Public Liability Insurance in a sum not less than $20,000,000.00 or such other amount that Council shall determine from time to time.

QUESTION ON NOTICE:
Councillor Curran requested further information from Acting Director of Infrastructure Services regarding infrastructure fees and charges to community groups.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Original Officer Recommendation:
That Council, as Assessment Manager, REFUSE the development application for a Development Permit for Operational Work to erect an Advertising Device (third-party digital billboard) on land at Tandur Road, Kybong, QLD, 4570, for the following reasons: 

  1. The proposed development does not comply with Purpose and Overall Outcome (1), Overall Outcome (2)(d), Performance Outcome PO9(a), and Performance Outcome PO9(f) of the Advertising Devices Code of the Planning Scheme. The subject site is zoned Industry Investigation Area, which is not an appropriately zoned area for a Third Party Advertising Device, the surrounding locality is not distinctly used for commercial or industrial purposes, and the proposed Electronic Billboard would detract from the overall rural character and amenity of the locality. 
  2. The proposed development does not comply with Overall Outcome (2)(b) and Performance Outcome PO9(b) of the Advertising Devices Code. The locality has a distinct rural landscape character with minimal intrusion of advertising devices and the proposed Electronic Billboard is incompatible with that character. 
  3. The proposed development does not comply with Performance Outcome PO9(c) of the Advertising Devices Code. The proposed device is oriented toward and directly visible from the new Bruce Highway motorway corridor, which falls within the intended scope of the Third Party Advertising Device Exclusion Area provisions, the mapping of which pre-dates the construction of the new motorway. 
  4.  The proposed development does not comply with Performance Outcome PO9(d) of the Advertising Devices Code. The proposed Electronic Billboard, with a sign face area of 36m² (double the acceptable outcome maximum of 18m²) and a height of 8m (exceeding the acceptable outcome maximum of 7m), is of a form, size and scale that would dominate the rural and natural environment in which it is located.
  5. The proposed development does not comply with Overall Outcome (2)(f), Performance Outcome PO9(d), AO6.3 and Performance Outcome PO6 of the Advertising Devices Code. The proposed Electronic Billboard, being a large illuminated LED device visible from and oriented toward a high-speed motorway corridor operating at 110km/h, is reasonably likely to distract motorists and create a traffic hazard for users of the Bruce Highway. This is consistent with the advice of the Department of Transport and Main Roads, which has on multiple occasions advised that the device is reasonably likely to create a traffic hazard for the motorway within the meaning of section 43 of the Transport Infrastructure Act 1994, having regard to the low ambient light conditions at the location, the considerable display area of the device. The submitted Traffic Report by Modus Transport and Traffic Engineering does not conclude that the proposal will not distract drivers or create a traffic hazard for road users.
  6. The proposed development does not comply with Performance Outcome PO5 of the Advertising Devices Code. The proposed illuminated LED device is located in a zone that does not permit illuminated advertising under AO5.1, and the illumination of the device in this low ambient light rural setting is not appropriate to the setting, is likely to cause nuisance to surrounding rural land uses, and is likely to create a traffic safety hazard for motorists on the Bruce Highway.
In accordance with Section 45(5)(b) of the Planning Act 2016, Officers can have regard to ‘Other Relevant Matters’. The following relevant matters are considered to support the proposed development application’s refusal:
  1. TMR advice that states its preference the proposal Advertising Device not be approved, identifying it as presenting "an unnecessary impact on road safety through distraction for drivers of a type that is generally not expected in such a locality, particularly at night.".
  2. The Third Party Advertising Device Exclusion Area mapping identified in Figure 1 of the Advertising Devices Code was prepared prior to the construction of the new Bruce Highway. The new Bruce Highway, which now forms the eastern boundary of the subject site, is a motorway-standard road operating at 110km/h and the type of corridor the exclusion area provisions were intended to protect from intrusive third party advertising. Had the mapping been prepared following the motorway's construction, the new Bruce Highway corridor would, in Council's assessment, have been captured within the exclusion area. The intent of the exclusion area provisions is plainly applicable to this site, and this provides strong independent support for refusal reinforcing the non-compliance with PO9(c).
  3. The relevant matters put forward by the applicant are not considered sufficient to overcome the non-compliances identified above.

At all times 
17 
The sign operator is to enter into a commercial agreement with Gympie Regional Council (at the expense of the sign operator) for the dedication of advertising operational screen time (for council/community promotional purposes) for the advertising device, which includes the following provisions –  
  • A minimum of 16.6% of the signage time is to be provided for council/community promotional purposes (i.e. a minimum of 1 ad out of the six (6) ads);
  • Annual Renewal;
  • Exposure times; 
  • Time frame for the advertising device to be updated to depict a new council/community advertisement;
  • Be provided to the sign operator at no expense to the sign operator; and
  • Be provided to the sign operator in a format suitable for display on the screen.
 
Prior to commencement of operational works and to be maintained at all times thereafter. 
Landscape Requirements 
18 
Landscaping must be provided around the advertising device to screen the supporting structures and built form of the device. Landscaping must comprise a mix of ground covers and small to medium shrubs such that all supporting structures of the device are visually screened.  
Prior to commencement of operational works and to be maintained at all times thereafter.  

19 
A detailed Landscape Plan is to be submitted to Council demonstrating compliance with Condition (18) above, and in accordance with the specifications and standards required in the Planning Scheme Policy SC6.1.10 – Landscape Plans and Plant Species.  
In conjunction with a development permit for operational works and prior to commencement of operational works. 
 
Other conditions 
20 
(a) The owner must, prior to the commencement of operation of the advertising device, provide Council with: 
  1. A current 24-hour contact telephone number for a responsible person who has authority to act on complaints relating to the device; and
  2. A current email address for the lodgement of written complaints. 

(b) The owner must notify Council of any change to the contact details provided under (a) within five (5) business days of the change. 

(c) Upon receipt of a written notice from Council identifying a complaint regarding luminance levels, display content, or any other matter relating to the operation of the device, the owner must: 
  1. Acknowledge receipt of the notice within twenty-four (24) hours; and 
  2. Investigate and, where required, take corrective action within forty-eight (48) hours of receipt of the notice, or such longer period as agreed in writing with Council. 
 
(d) Where Council reasonably considers, following receipt of a complaint, that the device presents an immediate risk to public safety or amenity, Council may direct the owner in writing to cease operation of the device. The owner must comply with such a direction immediately upon receipt. 
 
(a) Prior to commencement of operation.
(b), (c) and (d) At all times. 

 Council notes the reasons for this decision is as follows:
  • Pursuant to Section 45(5)(b) of the Planning Act 2016, the following relevant matters allow for the development application to be supported, despite conflicts with the Gympie Regional Council Planning Scheme 2013:
    • Public Good and Benefit:
      • The advertising device can be utilised during disaster management responses to notify the public of the status of natural disasters occurring in the region.
    • Tourism Benefits:
      • The advertising device can be utilised to promote local attractions, and tourist activities at a key gateway location into the Gympie Region.
    • Community and Local Economic Benefit:
      • The advertising device can be utilised to promote local businesses, and community and/or Council events.



Carried

     The overall plan for the Rural Fire Levy special charge is as follows: 
           i.  The service, facility or activity for which the plan is made is the funding of the ongoing provision and maintenance of rural firefighting equipment, operations

          iii. The estimated cost of carrying out the overall plan is $299,750
          iv. The estimated time for carrying out the overall plan is one year ending on 30 June 2027. 
     
     The rateable land to be levied the special charge specifically benefits from the fire emergency response capability that is provided by the rural fire brigades, which capability would be substantially (if not completely) diminished if the rural fire brigades did not receive the funding provided to them by Council as a direct consequence of the levying of the special charge. M24/7/2026 
Moved Cr Gordon Maudsley
Seconded Cr Warren McEwan

That Council, as Assessment Manager, APPROVE the development application for a Development Permit for a Material Change of Use to establish a Function Facility, Short-Term Accommodation, and Tourist Park on land at 908 Kandanga Creek Road, Kandanga Creek, Qld, 4570 for the following reasons: 
  1. The assessment of the proposed development against the Gympie Regional Council Planning Scheme 2013 confirms compliance with all relevant assessment benchmarks.
  2. The approved Tourist Park provides small-scale visitor accommodation, which is an anticipated and acceptable use within the Rural Zone, and complements the proposed Function Facility land use.
  3. The Short-Term Accommodation provides small-scale visitor accommodation, which does not detract from the rural or agricultural viability of the subject site, and further complements the proposed Function Facility land use. 
  4. Subject to the recommended conditions of approval, including the appointment of an event manager for the Function Facility, the development can appropriately mitigate potential amenity impacts. 
  5. The development demonstrates compliance with relevant noise criteria, supported by operational conditions that effectively restrict noise generation and require onsite management for the Function Facility. 
  6. The proposal will be serviced by all infrastructure required to support the development. 
  7. The proposed development is consistent with the State Planning Policy 2017, provided the applicant obtains and implements a Flood Evacuation Management Plan prepared by a suitably qualified person, to minimise the risk to an acceptable and tolerable level.

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley

M32/7/2026 
Moved Cr Mick Curran
Seconded Cr Warren McEwan

That Council:
  1. Endorses the renewal of the Aquatic Centre Management Services Agreement with Belgravia Health and Leisure Group Pty Ltd as trustee for Belgravia Leisure Unit Trust, for one (1) further three (3) year period, commencing 1 September 2026 and expiring 31 August 2029, noting the following essential terms:
      1. The contract is for the continued management of the Goomeri Public Pool, Gympie Aquatic Recreation Centre, Kandanga Public Pool and Tin Can Bay Public Pool;
      2. The amount payable for the period 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2027 period is $799,551 excluding GST.

  3. Notes that Council officers will continue to monitor and review future sustainable management options for Council’s aquatic facilities during the renewal term.

Carried

ORIGINAL OFFICER RECOMMENDATION:
That Council consider the following motions to be submitted to the Local Government Association of Queensland:

Motion 1 - That the LGAQ calls on the State Government to review and update planning legislation, the State Planning Policy and associated guidance to ensure land use definitions and assessment frameworks appropriately recognise emerging technologies and infrastructure, including electric vehicle charging stations, and provide consistent application across local government areas.

Motion 2 - That the LGAQ calls on the State Government to advocate for, and work in partnership with the Commonwealth Government, to improve alignment between workforce strategies, regional economic development priorities, and migration and visa settings, including consideration of targeted regional migration pathways, to support sustainable growth and service delivery across Queensland local government areas.

Motion 3 - That the LGAQ calls on the State Government to retain biodiversity, environmental and natural hazard State Interests within the SPP to ensure consistent statewide planning outcomes, reduce legal and financial risks for councils, and enable local governments to appropriately identify and protect matters of environmental significance.

Motion 4 - That the Local Government Association of Queensland (LGAQ) calls on the Queensland Government to:
  1. Renew or extend funding for Regional Resource Recovery Coordinator (RRRC) positions across Queensland beyond the current funding period;
  2. Recognise RRRC positions as a critical mechanism for delivering the Queensland Waste Management and Resource Recovery Strategy and associated regional waste and resource recovery plans;
  3. Provide ongoing funding certainty to enable regional councils to continue collaborating on strategic waste and resource recovery initiatives, infrastructure planning, market development, education programs and circular economy opportunities; and
  4. Support local governments to achieve the Queensland Government’s waste reduction, recycling and resource recovery targets through coordinated regional implementation.

Motion 5 - That the LGAQ calls on the Federal Government to 
  1. Abandon the proposed changes to disaster recovery funding arrangements to reduce Commonwealth support for disaster-impacted councils and communities which were announced on 5 June 2026.
  2. Retain disaster recovery funding settings that are fair, certain and sustainable for Queensland local governments and ensure that any reform of disaster recovery funding arrangements does not reduce the overall level of Commonwealth support available to disaster-impacted local governments and communities, and further advocates that any revised funding framework: 
    1. Guarantees that no local government or community is financially disadvantaged under any revised disaster recovery funding framework; 
    2. Maintains or increases Commonwealth funding contributions that recognise Queensland's disproportionate exposure to natural disasters and the critical role local government plays in restoring essential public infrastructure and community services; 
    3. Undertake genuine consultation with local government before finalising any replacement framework; 
    4. Restores, protects and grows untied Commonwealth funding to local government, including Financial Assistance Grants, to strengthen councils' capacity to prepare for, respond to and recover from increasingly frequent and severe disaster events; and 
    5. Increases investment in disaster mitigation and resilience infrastructure to reduce future recovery costs and strengthen community resilience.

Recommendation 1
That Council resolves to approve the exception referred to in Chapter 6 Section 236(1)(c)(vi) of the Local Government Regulation 2012 allowing Council to "dispose (through leasing) the subject land, other than by tender or auction, if the disposal is for the purpose of a lease for a telecommunication tower".

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

M21/9/2026 
Moved  Cr Jess Milne
Seconded  Cr Warren McEwan

Recommendation 2
That Council resolves to rescind the resolution made on 24 January 2024 in relation to item no. 8.2 of the Ordinary Meeting Agenda and offer a new Trustee Lease over part of Lot 28 SP103952 located at the Beagle Campground site to Telstra Limited in Council's standard commercial telecommunications trustee lease format, to include the following terms and conditions:
  1. Term of Lease - 10 years;
  2. Annual Rent - $2,000 plus GST.  Rent will be increased annually on the anniversary of the commencement date at a fixed rate of 2%;
  3. Use - Telecommunications facility;
  4. Public Liability Insurance - the Trustee Lessee to hold Public Liability Insurance in a sum not less than $20,000,000 or such other amount that Council shall determine from time to time; and
  5. Costs - the Lessee will be responsible for:
    1.  all legal fees in relation to finalising the new lease to a maximum of $2,000.00 plus GST;
    2.  all costs associated with obtaining a lease area survey plan;
    3.  all Titles Queensland registration costs; and
    4. all costs relating to satisfaction of Native Title Act compliance.

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

That Council

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Jensen informed the meeting that she is a member of the Gympie Women's Shed and therefore volunteers to leave the room for this item. Councillor Jensen left the room at 9:08am. 

Councillor Curran discloses a friendship with the board chairman and that they go on a yearly fishing trip and share minor shares in a syndicate of two racehorses. Councillor Curran notes that for transparency he declares this interest but intends to stay in the room and vote on the matter.

Councillor Maudsley declares to the room that he is the vice president of the Friends of Amamoor, that has an access agreement with the Rattler Rail Company for a portion of the area at the Amamoor Train Station. Councilor Maudsley declares this interest but would like to stay in the room and votes on the matter. 

M19/9/2026 
Moved  Cr Mick Curran
Seconded  Cr Jess Milne

Set the standing orders aside and allow for a deputation. 

Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran, Councillor Jensen, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: None

M18/9/2026 
Moved  Mayor Glen Hartwig
Seconded  Cr Gordon Maudsley

That Council:

  1. Confirms it is satisfied with the evidence provided by Queensland Rail Limited via correspondence dated 21 September 2026 as to its capacity to enter a freehold lease with Gympie Regional Council over Part of Lot 264 SP103062, 42 Tozer Street, Gympie; and
  2. Resolves to enter into a freehold lease with Queensland Rail Limited over Part of Lot 264 SP103062, 42 Tozer Street, Gympie, to include the following terms and conditions:
    1. Term of lease – 10 years;
    2. Annual rental - $1.00 plus GST (if demanded)
    3. Use – Community use associated with the operation of a ‘Men’s Shed’ and/or ‘Women’s Shed’ or similar; and
    4. Lessee to provide confirmation it holds $20,000,000 public liability insurance.


Carried

FOR: Mayor Hartwig, Councillor Lahn, Councillor Maudsley, Councillor Warnes, Councillor McEwan, Councillor Polley
AGAINST: Councillor Milne, Councillor Curran

Councillor Jensen returned to the room at 9:59am.
